correctness.rationale: The four published branch probabilities give a connected N-state graph consisting of a cycle of N-2 edges and two leaves for every integer N>=7 and 0<theta<pi/N. Its reversible sine weights follow by edgewise trigonometric detailed balance. At A1, the two positive two-step returns have displacements 4theta+4alpha and 8alpha, impossible to phase-match for any nonzero integer spatial Fourier mode when theta/pi is irrational. The strict spectral-radius bound for each fixed mode, finite-chain angular convergence and Fourier approximation yield the stated weak laws. Rational theta/pi confines every position to a finite circle subgroup translate. Finite numerical checks are supplementary; no uniform Fourier decay or total-variation convergence is claimed.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The prior strong Knudsen laws have the spatial Haar property as an initial assumption and thus do not imply convergence of the position from a deterministic boundary point. The 2022 global mixing theorem is for the full angular continuum and excludes rational parameters, so cannot subsume conditional convergence on a finite rational-angle class.

The claimed Fourier contraction and the two parity-resolved joint limits are logically stronger than pathwise denseness and distinct from whole-space mixing.

value.rationale: A point-source spatial equidistribution theorem for a natural random billiard is mathematically different from the previous pathwise density result: finite angular classes do not prevent Haar spatial limits. The theorem gives a complete irrational/rational arithmetic boundary and explicit even/odd joint limiting measures despite a globally nonmixing rational reflection parameter. This is a motivated statistical classification rather than a small numerical refinement or an arbitrary parameter slice; the N>=7 family is the full simple rational parameter ladder below the original alpha<pi/6 range.
